articles.title: Broken Link Checking for Docs Sites: Build-Time Checks Plus Live Monitoring
articles.excerpt: Documentation sites are hard on links. They're full of cross-references between pages, anchors to specific sections, links to API references, code repositories, changelogs and third-party docs, and al…
articles.body: Documentation sites are hard on links. They're full of cross-references between pages, anchors to specific sections, links to API references, code repositories, changelogs and third-party docs, and all of those move. Pages get renamed when the product changes, versions get archived, and the external projects you link to restructure their own docs. A reader who follows a "see Configuration" link and lands on a 404 in the middle of a task is a frustrated reader, and often becomes a support ticket. The good news is that docs teams have better tools for this than most websites, because docs are usually built from source files. The catch is that build-time checks only catch some problems.

articles.body: On 21 October 2026 the PHP security team released versions that fix two critical vulnerabilities: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 . Both can allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), and both are rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0. The release had been announced a day earlier; when details leaked the same day, the fix shipped slightly ahead of the planned time. This post explains both vulnerabilities based on the official advisories, sums up who is at risk and what helps until you can update, and ends with what I did on my own server, step by step. There are no attack instructions here; everything is written from the defender's side.

articles.title: A DOI match is not an evidence check: design a clearer research-assistant contract
articles.excerpt: A DOI match should identify a paper, not certify a sentence. If you are building a research assistant, keep those two jobs separate in your data model and in the UI. Disclosure: I work on LitSource, a…
articles.body: A DOI match should identify a paper, not certify a sentence. If you are building a research assistant, keep those two jobs separate in your data model and in the UI. Disclosure: I work on LitSource, a biomedical literature and reference-checking product. This article was drafted and published with an AI agent. The examples below are a proposed application contract, not results from a benchmark or a claim of clinical validation. Three questions, three fields A bibliography checker can answer whether a reference resembles a scholarly record. That does not answer whether the paper supports a particular statement. Even a relevant paper may concern a different population, intervention, outcome or study setting.

articles.body: What I Built I built SlothSort AI, a local AI-powered file organizer that helps users organize messy folders without manually opening, understanding, renaming, and sorting every file. SlothSort AI scans a selected folder and supports files such as PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, and XLSX. It reads the file contents and uses local AI to understand the documents and help classify them. The goal is simple: let AI handle the boring file organization while you do less work. 🦥 Demo 🎥 Demo video: Coming soon The application is currently being developed and tested locally using Streamlit and Ollama. Code SlothSort AI GitHub Repository How I Built It I built SlothSort AI using Python, Streamlit, and Ollama. For local AI processing, I use the Llama 3.2 3B open-weight model through Ollama.

articles.title: Notes from a 2 AM On-Call: Supabase Realtime Connection Reset Under Next.js SSR Load
articles.excerpt: Notes from a 2 AM On-Call: Supabase Realtime Connection Reset Under Next.js SSR Load The Failure Symptom [supabase-js] RealtimeClient connection error: Error: WebSocket closed with code 1006 [Next.js]…
articles.body: Notes from a 2 AM On-Call: Supabase Realtime Connection Reset Under Next.js SSR Load The Failure Symptom [supabase-js] RealtimeClient connection error: Error: WebSocket closed with code 1006 [Next.js] TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'channel') [Vercel] Function invocation timeout after 10s Production dashboard went dark at 1:47 AM. No client errors. Server logs showed Supabase Realtime subscriptions silently dropping after 8-12 seconds under concurrent Server Component render load. The kicker? Local dev was flawless. Staging with 10 concurrent users worked. Production with 200+ simultaneous SSR requests collapsed.

articles.body: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney conducts botany experiments on the ISS. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Watkins) Growing plants in space? Yes indeed! In this snapshot — captured by NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins, commander of SpaceX 's Crew-13 mission to the ISS — we can see fellow NASA spaceflyer Luke Delaney hard at work aboard the ISS. articles.title: When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines (and an Artemis III update)
articles.excerpt: NASA has updated the timeline for its Artemis III mission and mapped out the expected progress for SpaceX and Blue Origin's respective moon landers.
articles.body: NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program . During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon . A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027.

articles.title: Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight: Here's the best time to spot shooting stars
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight (Oct. 21-22) in the light of a waxing moon. Here's what to expect from one of Autumn's greatest natural light shows.
articles.body: Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show? The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061. Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA . However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

articles.body: Generative AI has changed what a malicious email looks like. Messages that once gave themselves away through clumsy wording, generic pretexts, and reused templates now arrive fluent, personalized, and unique to each recipient, and the behavioral signals email filters have relied on for years are fading as a result. Proofpoint shared several examples of the shift at its Protect 2026 conference.

articles.title: Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter?
articles.excerpt: A Russian satellite just conducted a startlingly close approach of a private American Earth-observing satellite. What was the goal of the controversial maneuver?
articles.body: A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit. A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

articles.title: I split Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT into work, home, and casual, and it’s a mixed bag
articles.excerpt: Here's what happened when I assigned distinct roles to Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT. This setup was a double-edged sword.
articles.body: Credit: Thanh Nguyen / Android Authority The explosion of LLMs, while intended to simplify our lives, has actually created a new flavor of chaos. Dozens of AI browser tabs and app windows crawl over my screen, whether I’m using a computer, a tablet, or a phone. To make matters worse, I admit that I can’t live without them now. I’ve long tried to leverage the collective versatility of AI models by continuously hopping between them. This approach got my work done, but at the cost of messy conversation boxes and occasional miscommunication. I didn’t blame any of them for such inconveniences — I contaminated their context windows myself with all kinds of questions, from work queries to sudden breezes of thought.
